findings.title: Lost-update race condition on retryCount increment
findings.body: Both the else branch (line 184) and the catch block (line 195) update retryCount via a read-modify-write: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`. The `reminder.retryCount` value was read by the initial `findMany` at the start of the handler. If a second instance of this cron handler (or an overlapping invocation) has already updated the same row between the read and this update, the second writer will overwrite the first writer's increment using the stale value. The net retryCount will be off by at least one, causing premature (or never-triggered) deletion. The fix is to use Prisma's atomic increment: `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`, which does not require reading the current value. This is especially relevant because the cleanup at the top of the handler (line 29) will delete the row once `retryCount > 1`, so a lost update can directly cause data loss.

findings.title: deleteMany cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders with retryCount > 1
findings.body: The new OR branch in the cleanup deleteMany (lines 38-42) deletes any WorkflowReminder with `retryCount > 1` regardless of `method`. This handler is only responsible for SMS scheduling, so it should not be deleting EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders. While the current codebase only increments retryCount for SMS, the column is on the shared `WorkflowReminder` model and any future code path that bumps retryCount for other methods (or pre-existing data from another env) would be silently deleted by this SMS-only cron. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount branch to scope the cleanup correctly.

findings.title: Catch block increments retryCount for transient errors, not just scheduling failures
findings.body: The catch block (lines 189-199) wraps the entire try body, which includes non-Twilio work: `prisma.profile.findFirst`, `getBookerBaseUrl`, `customTemplate`, `smsReminderTemplate`, and `bookingMetadataSchema.parse`. A transient failure in any of these (DB blip, malformed booking metadata, template variable missing) will increment retryCount exactly the same as a permanent Twilio failure like an invalid phone number. After 2 such transient errors the reminder is permanently deleted even though `twilio.scheduleSMS` was never reached or would have succeeded. The retry-counting should be scoped to the `twilio.scheduleSMS` call (and its returned falsy case), not the whole try block, or transient errors should not count toward the retry budget.

findings.title: Else branch unreachable when message or sendTo is empty, so retryCount never advances
findings.body: The else branch that increments retryCount (lines 178-187) is nested inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. If `message` is empty/null or `sendTo` is missing, neither the success path nor the retryCount increment runs, but `scheduled` remains false. Such reminders will never have retryCount incremented, so they will never be cleaned up by the new `retryCount > 1` branch and will sit indefinitely (only deleted when `scheduledDate <= now`). This was a pre-existing latent issue but is now more relevant because the new cleanup logic was specifically introduced to prevent indefinite retention of unprocessable reminders. The empty-message/missing-sendTo case should also bump retryCount (or be cleaned up) so the same retry budget applies.

findings.title: No tests added for the new retry-count cleanup and increment behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces a non-trivial state machine: a new column, a new cleanup branch (`retryCount > 1`), and two new retryCount increments (else + catch). None of these behaviors are covered by tests. At minimum, tests should cover: (1) reminders are deleted after the retryCount threshold; (2) reminders below the threshold are kept; (3) successful scheduleSMS updates `scheduled=true` and does not bump retryCount; (4) falsy return from scheduleSMS bumps retryCount; (5) thrown errors bump retryCount. Without these, future refactors can silently regress the retry budget.

findings.title: Off-by-one between description and implementation: 2 attempts before deletion, not "twice failed"
findings.body: The PR description says "after scheduling failed twice we delete the workflow reminder", but the implementation starts retryCount at 0 and deletes when `retryCount > 1`, meaning the row is deleted after the second failure only on the *third* cron invocation (the third invocation's cleanup deletes it because retryCount is now 2). The initial state counts as the first attempt, so the reminder is actually scheduled twice before being given up on. If the intent is "after 2 failed attempts", the description is accurate but ambiguous; if the intent is "try once, then retry once, then give up", that's what the code does. Either way, a comment near the cleanup query documenting the semantics (`retryCount > 1` means "has already been retried once") would prevent future confusion. This is also a documentation defect because the comment on line 28 ("delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date") was not updated to reflect the new OR branch.
